# Secondary protocol

These retrospective analyses supplement the frozen resolved-outcome test. Compare the same model families using log loss in natural units, averaged first over registrations within a course/module and then equally over courses/modules. Include the class frequencies of the relevant training partition as a reference. The model comparisons are descriptive.

* Portugal, UCI 697. Use all released statuses in alphabetical order (Dropout, Enrolled, Graduate). Hold out one course at a time. Fit multinomial models with the primary features, preprocessing and each outer fold's previously chosen family settings. Those settings used resolved outcomes from other courses. Hold model probabilities fixed and score three labels, recorded dropout versus the other two, and absence of recorded graduation versus graduation. On the original resolved rows, also divide dropout probability by dropout plus graduate probability and score the original conditional question. Compare average predictions with observed dropout rates by course for the primary and all-label fits. A signed gap is predicted minus observed. Summaries use absolute gaps and retain cell sizes.
* United Kingdom, Open University Learning Analytics Dataset, UCI 349, 2013–2014. Refit the same families locally using registration lead time, number of previous attempts, and studied credits. At the end of day zero require registration by then and no recorded exit on or before then. Outcome is final Withdrawn versus Pass, Fail or Distinction. No grade, future interaction, exit date, learner, module or presentation identifier enters a model. Reserve October 2014 (2014J) for testing. Exclude February 2014 from development because some modules could still be running in October. Remove every 2014J learner from development, even if their test registration is ineligible. Use February 2013 to fit and October 2013 to choose settings by equal-module loss, excluding October 2013 learners from the February tuning fit. Refit on both 2013 presentations. This offline tuning split orders starts only. Both development presentations finish before the outer test. Treat each registration as an observation.
* Within each refit shuffle training positions deterministically (seed 42), without using labels. Source row numbers are zero-based identifiers for joins, never dates or predictors. Save held-out probabilities, settings and per-course losses and gaps. Use an independent scoring script to rejoin the original labels and recompute grouped metrics. No new superiority test or choice of a winning target.
